title: Identity Disclosure
description: The wearable device (P1) shares raw sensor telemetry data (heart rate, step counts, GPS position, timestamps) with the user (EE1) without any authentication or privacy controls. This allows the user to directly identify and track the wearer's physical location and biometric state.

title: Data Processing and Re-identification
description: Upon receiving the raw telemetry data, the wearable device (P1) processes this information to generate a unique user profile or location history. This processing step enables the device to link the raw sensor data to a specific individual's identity and track their movements over time.

title: Device ID Disclosure
description: The wearable device (P1) shares its unique identifier (device id) with the companion app (P2) during the sync process. This allows the app to uniquely identify the user and associate all subsequent data (exercise sessions, GPS traces) with that specific individual, enabling targeted tracking and profiling.
assumptions: The device is configured to transmit device id to the app.

title: Sensitive Data Exposure
description: The wearable device (P1) shares sensitive personal data (exercise sessions, GPS traces) with the companion app (P2). This data is highly sensitive and, once exposed, can be used to infer private information about the user's health, location history, and physical activity patterns.
assumptions: The device is configured to transmit exercise sessions and GPS traces to the app.

title: Data Linking via Meta-data
description: The data flow (DF2) transmits meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., 'Wearable Device' and 'Companion Mobile App') to the destination (P2). This allows the app to link the data it receives to the specific wearable device, enabling the app to track the user's movements and behavior across different devices and over time.
assumptions: The app receives and processes the meta-data identifying the source device.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The companion app (P2) receives and processes the shared data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, timestamps). By storing this data, the app creates a persistent record of the user's physical activity and location history, which can be used for behavioral analysis, advertising, or other purposes that may compromise privacy.
assumptions: The app stores the received data for processing.

title: User Identity Disclosure
description: The user (EE1) manually logs calorie intake, meals, and weight entries. This action inherently reveals the user's identity and personal data (calories, meals, weight) to the Companion Mobile App (P2).

title: Data Linking and Identification
description: The data flow (DF3) transmits user identity and personal data (calories, meals, weight) in transit. The act of sharing this data with the destination (P2) allows the destination to link or identify the user based on the data content.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The destination (P2) receives the user's personal data (calories, meals, weight) and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat, potentially leading to unauthorized access or misuse of the user's information.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: The mobile app (P2) is configured to write health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) to the Health Log Store (DS1) without any user consent or explicit permission. This unauthorized sharing of sensitive personal health information (PHI) constitutes a direct privacy threat.
assumptions: The app has no user consent mechanism or privacy policy for this specific data flow.

title: Data Processing Threat
description: The Health Log Store (DS1) receives the health logs and processes them for storage. If the store is not configured with appropriate access controls or encryption, it may store or expose the health data in a way that causes a privacy threat.
assumptions: The store's internal processing logic does not include necessary safeguards for PHI.

title: Location Data Exposure
description: The source element (App) shares GPS location traces with the destination element (Location History Store) without any authentication or encryption, making the data accessible to any party who can access the destination.

title: Data Processing for Location Tracking
description: The destination element (Location History Store) receives the location data and stores it in a way that allows for future location tracking and profiling of the user.

title: Data Leakage
description: The source element (DataStore) shares sensitive health data (calories, weight, exercise logs) with the analytics service without appropriate access controls or encryption.

title: Data Linking
description: The data flow transmits metadata about the parties involved (e.g., user ID, session ID) which could be used to link or identify individuals across different sessions.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (Process) processes the health data in a way that causes privacy threats, such as aggregating data across sessions to create a profile of the user's health condition.

title: Data Exfiltration
description: The data store (DS2) shares location history data with the analytics service (P3) without any explicit consent or authorization from the data subjects. This constitutes a direct data breach where sensitive personal location data is transferred to an untrusted third party.
assumptions: The data store has no mechanism to verify the identity or consent of the data subjects before sharing the data.

title: Data Linking and Identification
description: The data flow (DF7) transmits location history data in a format that allows the analytics service (P3) to link multiple data points together. This enables the creation of a unique user profile based on location patterns, which can be used to identify individuals and track their movements across different sessions.
assumptions: The data format used in the flow is generic and does not include metadata that could be used to uniquely identify the data subjects.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The analytics service (P3) processes the received location history data to derive daily routine and movement patterns. This processing step involves aggregating and analyzing the data, which could lead to the creation of detailed behavioral profiles that are not necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: The analytics service has a clear, limited purpose for processing the data and does not store it indefinitely.

title: Data Leakage
description: The source element (Process P3) shares health-condition risk indicators and trend flags with the destination element (Process P2) without appropriate access controls or encryption. This allows unauthorized access to sensitive health data.
assumptions: The source element does not enforce data minimization or encryption requirements.

title: Data In Transit
description: The data flow (DF8) transmits health-condition risk indicators and trend flags over the network. This exposes the data to potential interception or metadata-based identification attacks.
assumptions: The network is secure and no third-party intermediaries are involved.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (Process P2) receives the health data and processes it in a way that causes a threat, such as storing it in a way that allows future unauthorized access or using it for non-health-related purposes.
assumptions: The destination element does not implement proper access controls or data retention policies.

title: Inference of Condition Indicators
description: The source element (Process P2) shares data about inferred condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) to the user. This act of sharing causes the threat because the user may not understand the nature of the data or the implications of sharing it, leading to potential misuse or unauthorized access.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF9) transmits data about the user's inferred condition indicators. This data-centric threat arises because the meta-data associated with the data flow (e.g., the fact that the user is being tracked for health trends) can be used to link or identify the user across different systems or devices, even if the user's identity is not explicitly shared.

title: Processing of Inferred Health Data
description: The destination element (User/ExternalEntity EE1) receives and processes the inferred condition indicators. This action causes the threat because the user may not be aware of the specific health data being processed, leading to potential privacy violations such as data aggregation, profiling, or unauthorized sharing of inferred health conditions.

title: Data Sharing
description: The source element (Process P3) shares analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset with the external entity (Cloud Hosting Provider EE2). This act of sharing causes the threat because the data is exposed to a third party without appropriate access controls or encryption.

title: Data in Transit
description: The data-centric threat arises at the data flow (DF10) where the data is transmitted between the source (P3) and the destination (EE2). The threat is that the data in transit is potentially identifiable or linked to the parties involved, allowing for potential tracking or profiling.

title: Data Processing
description: At the destination element (Cloud Hosting Provider EE2), the threat arises because the entity receives and processes the health and location dataset. This processing may involve storing, analyzing, or using the data in ways that compromise privacy, such as re-identification or aggregation.
